title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed page, numbered '- 30 - IX', of Grothendieck's SGA 7 I, Exposé IX ('Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), §3. It concerns the global case. S is a Dedekind scheme with function field K, and A_K is an abelian variety over K.

3.2.1 makes three points about the Néron model A of A_K over S:
- It is defined by the same universal property (the Néron mapping property) as in the local case of 1.1.
- Its existence, and the fact that it is separated of finite type, reduce at once to the local case.
- For every closed point s, S' = Spec O_{S,s} is a trait (a spectrum of a discrete valuation ring), and A×_S S' is the Néron model of A_K over S'. In other words, Néron models are compatible with localization.

Proof of Theorem 3.2. The theorem characterizes semi-abelian (semistable) reduction:
- (i) The identity components of the fibres of A have unipotent rank 0, i.e. are semi-abelian.
- (ii) There exists a smooth separated S-group scheme G of finite type with generic fibre A_K whose fibre identity components are semi-abelian.
Setting G = A gives (i)⇒(ii). For (ii)⇒(i), the canonical map G→A given by the Néron property is an open immersion by 3.1 e), so the fibre identity components agree.

Corollary 3.3 (stability of semistable reduction under base change). Suppose A has semi-abelian fibre identity components. Let f: S'→S be a dominant morphism of Dedekind schemes, K'/K the corresponding extension of function fields, and A' the Néron model of A_{K'}. Then the unique morphism u: A×_S S' → A' extending the identity on generic fibres is an open immersion. Hence A°×_S S' ≅ A'°.

Proof: apply 3.2 over S' with G = A×_S S'. This is smooth with generic fibre A_{K'}, and its fibre identity components are base changes of semi-abelian groups, so they are semi-abelian.

The mathematics serves the semistable reduction theory of SGA 7 IX. The page has nothing to do with the de Rham/divided-power material on the neighbouring pages; it is evidently a stray SGA 7 typescript sheet filed in this dossier.
errors: No mathematical errors. 'Dominant' is needed so that S'→S induces a field extension K→K'. In the proof one tacitly uses that a base change of a semi-abelian group over a field is semi-abelian and that A×_S S' is smooth and separated of finite type; both are immediate.

ideas.what: Néron model over a Dedekind base: existence via reduction to the local case, compatibility with localization at closed points
Semi-abelian reduction iff some smooth group model with semi-abelian fibre identity components exists; such a model embeds openly in the Néron model
Identity component of the Néron model commutes with base change when reduction is semi-abelian

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript of published SGA 7 IX (3.2.1–3.3), which is standard and fully credited to Grothendieck. Its only oddity is archival: it is misfiled in the 1975–76 divided-power de Rham dossier.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription is essentially correct. '(ii)' in 'comme dans (ii)' is a handwritten correction over the typescript.
The pencil numbers '348' and '180' are archive foliation, not part of the text.
